blocks.h2: Venting a New Heater in an Older Evanston Home
blocks.body: Many older Evanston homes vent the furnace and water heater through the same masonry chimney. When a high-efficiency furnace is installed, it often gets its own plastic vent, leaving the water heater alone in a chimney sized for two. That can cause poor draft and condensation. When we replace your water heater, we check the draft and tell you whether the chimney needs a liner or whether a power-vent heater is the better choice.

blocks.h2: What Affects the Price of a New Water Heater
blocks.body: Size and fuel come first. In older Evanston homes, venting can be a big factor: a chimney liner or power-vent unit may be needed. Access, like steep stairs or a tight space, adds labor. Code updates like an expansion tank may apply. We check everything and quote one flat price.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Replacement Questions From Evanston Homeowners

items.q: What size water heater do I need?
items.answer: It depends on how many people live there and how many bathrooms you have. Most homes use 40 or 50 gallons.

items.q: Do I need a chimney liner?
items.answer: Sometimes, if the heater is the last appliance on an old chimney. We test the draft.

items.q: Can you replace it the same day?
Do you take the old one?
Should I get a bigger tank?
items.preview: Only if you run out often.
items.answer: Only if you run out of hot water often. A bigger tank costs more to keep hot.

items.q: Can you install a water heater on an upper floor?
items.answer: Yes, with a drain pan and proper venting to protect the rooms below.

items.q: How much does water heater replacement cost in Evanston?
items.preview: It depends on size, type and venting. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on size, fuel type, venting and access. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
